Continue up class 3 tread gaining roughly 800 ft into the Redoubt Glacier basin; Ouzel Lake, in this basin, is the most common first camp. From Ouzel Lake most parties relocate camp 3-4 hours further up onto the Redoubt Glacier saddle/col (~7,150 ft) for a high camp closer to the peaks — this leg is flat glacier travel with only minor, usually avoidable crevasse hazard in normal late-season conditions. From high camp, traverse roughly 2 miles east across snow/glacier beneath Easy Mox's south side toward the 'Col of the Wild,' the saddle between Easy and Hard (Southeast) Mox, finishing with a steep ~1,000 ft climb over notoriously unstable, sandy talus (loose rock is the dominant hazard on this whole upper approach — helmets on well before the col). From the Col of the Wild, ascend a ramp leading right past a snow patch into a gully, then scramble up and right (class 4, exposed enough that many parties belay it) toward a notch in the 'Ridge of Gendarmes.' A short sequence of ledges zig-zagging right-left-right leads through the notch; descend briefly to a small flat area and locate the correct gully leading to a high notch on the west ridge, which is the start of the roped climbing (two pitches of 5th class to the summit tower, then a final short, exposed class 3 scramble — stay roped — to the true summit). Water is available from the glacier/snowmelt and Ouzel Lake but not reliably along the upper ridge, so carry enough from camp.
wa_southeast_mox_peak_se_rib.descent_text: Descend by reversing the ascent line rather than any independent walk-off. From the true summit, most parties make three single-rope (30 m) rappels down the tower to a small, exposed high notch, then shorter rappels and downclimbing from that notch down the gully toward the glacier below — roughly three rappels to the notch in typical late-summer, snow-free conditions. Anchors along this line are almost entirely improvised rather than bolted: slung boulders, horns and pedestals wrapped with tat/cord, and the occasional jammed knot in a crack; a couple of the stations have accumulated enough old cord to look semi-permanent, but none should be trusted blindly and back-up/extend as needed. Bring a single 60 m rope; below the notch, expect to downclimb part of the gully. In seasons or conditions where a snow finger lingers in the descent gully, parties have needed far more — up to 9-10 shorter single-rope rappels interspersed with downclimbing to get through the same 400-ft gully system, because a lingering snow patch prevents a clean full-length pull; budget extra time and a plan B if you find snow still choking the gully. Known hazards on this descent: persistently loose, choss-prone rock (the Southeast Spire's rock quality is poor, and at least one incident involved a slab breaking loose during rope retrieval at the notch and striking a climber), ropes getting stuck when pulled through the loose gully, high exposure along the east ledges near the Ridge of Gendarmes, and fatigue/darkness on the lower-angle terrain given how long this climb runs. After reaching the glacier below the Col of the Wild, reverse the approach traverse back to your high camp (Redoubt Col/Ouzel Lake), then descend the Depot Creek climbers path past the falls — using the fixed handline again on the steep slab section — back to the trailhead.

waypoints.name: Depot Creek Road parking / trailhead
waypoints.note: Standard Depot Creek/Chilliwack Lake Road (Canada) trailhead for Mox Peaks/Redoubt approaches, via Depot Creek Falls and Ouzel Lake.
waypoints.directions: This trailhead is on the Canadian side of the border: follow Chilliwack Lake Road in BC to the abandoned logging spur at Depot Creek, where the parking sits at roughly 2,350 ft. From there the approach walks the old roadway grade, taking the left-hand fork, about a mile to the Monument 65 border marker, where you cross into North Cascades National Park and should sign in at the wilderness-permit kiosk.

waypoints.name: Monument 65 (US-Canada border)
waypoints.note: Border obelisk and North Cascades NP trail register/kiosk in old growth ~200 yd past the parking intersection; register for backcountry entry here.

waypoints.name: Depot Creek Falls handline/cable step
waypoints.note: Class 3 scramble past a ~967-ft waterfall on wet, slippery rock; an old cable/handline aids a steep, misty 8-ft rock step.

waypoints.name: Ouzel Lake camp
waypoints.note: Flat sandy/gravelly moraine benches above the lake outlet; established high-camp for Chilliwack-range climbs, ~9+ hrs / 3,550 ft above the cars.

waypoints.name: Redoubt Glacier saddle / high camp
waypoints.note: Broken buttress SW of Ouzel Lake tops out on rock outcrops at this glacier-edge saddle; rope up here for crevassed glacier travel, visibility often poor.

waypoints.name: Col of the Wild
waypoints.note: Contour ~2 mi of moderately steep snow on the Redoubt Glacier to this col between the Mox Peaks; final ~100 ft is loose talus over sand.

waypoints.name: Gendarme notch below SE Mox
waypoints.note: Class 2-3 ledges and a Class 4 headwall gain the high notch on the west side of the summit tower; rock is notably loose with high exposure.

waypoints.name: Southeast Mox Peak (Hard Mox) summit
waypoints.note: Three pitches up to 5.5 (mostly Class 3-4 on the final pitch) above the notch to the true summit; descend by downclimbing/short-rappelling back to the notch.

wa_vasiliki_ridge_standard.name: Standard Route (Ares Tower)
wa_vasiliki_ridge_standard.approach: Park at the unsigned 'Wine Spires' pullout on SR-20, about 3.7 miles east of Washington Pass (roughly 0.7 mile past the Cutthroat Lake Road turnoff, near milepost 166), at about 4,300 ft elevation. A boot path drops down loose, scree-covered talus into the trees, passes a trail register, and crosses Early Winters Creek on logs at about 4,080 ft. The trail then climbs steadily through forest, steepening between two side creeks, gaining roughly 3,700+ ft to Burgundy Col (~7,800 ft); a flat bench campsite ('the Bench,' ~6,460 ft) sits about halfway up and is the more common camp for this objective. Vasiliki Ridge and Ares Tower rise directly north of Burgundy Col and the Wine Spires camp area; from the bench or col, contour and scramble north along the ridge crest to reach the base of Ares Tower.
wa_vasiliki_ridge_standard.descent_text: Rappel from the fixed anchor at the Ares Tower summit down to the notch to retrieve stashed gear, then reverse the 4th-class ridge scramble and descend the Burgundy Col approach trail back to Early Winters Creek and the SR-20 pullout.

waypoints.name: Wine Spires / Burgundy Col pullout, SR-20
waypoints.note: Broad highway shoulder near milepost 166, ~3.7-4 mi east of Washington Pass; boot path drops from the pavement into trees toward Early Winters Creek.
waypoints.directions: Park at the unsigned Wine Spires pullout on SR-20, a broad highway shoulder about 3.7 miles east of Washington Pass and roughly 0.7 mile past the Cutthroat Lake Road turnoff, near milepost 166, at about 4,300 feet. North Cascades Highway 20 over Washington Pass is open only seasonally, typically from mid-April until a winter closure that comes between mid-November and early December, depending on weather and snowpack, so the pullout is inaccessible outside that window.

waypoints.name: Early Winters Creek log crossing
waypoints.note: Climbers' path crosses on logs almost immediately below the highway; last reliable, easy water until the Bench.

waypoints.name: The Ledge bivy
waypoints.note: Small established bivy shelf passed on the climbers' trail about two miles in, below the main Bench basin.

waypoints.name: The Bench
waypoints.note: Flat camping basin (~2 hrs up from the highway) used as a base camp for Wine Spires/Vasiliki Ridge objectives; last dependable water before the col in early season snowmelt.

waypoints.name: Burgundy Col
waypoints.note: Ridge-gain saddle ~3 mi/3-4 hrs from the highway; Vasiliki Tower sits immediately on the left entering the col — turn north here onto Vasiliki Ridge toward Ares Tower.

waypoints.name: Vasiliki Ridge Class 4 traverse
waypoints.note: Exposed, loose 4th-class ridge scrambling north from the col/Bench toward Ares Tower; rope up for parties uncomfortable with unroped exposure.

waypoints.name: Ares Tower summit
waypoints.note: Fixed rappel anchor at the true summit block (surveyed 8,202.8 ft); descend by rappelling into the notch to reverse the route.

bivy.name: Bench Camp — larch bench above the Wine Spires pullout
bivy.notes: The one genuinely used high camp on the Kangaroo Ridge side, reached by a steep switchbacking climbers' trail that gains roughly 2,000 ft from the highway. It is the sensible base for Vasiliki Ridge and Vasiliki Tower, for the west side of Juno Tower, and for linking two or three routes over a weekend rather than re-walking the approach each morning. Juno's east-side routes are a different problem — a 2.5 to 3.5 hour approach with a valley camp in Silver Star Creek — and this camp does not serve them. Bugs can be bad in July; water availability is what actually varies.
bivy.water: Present early in the season from snowmelt and the creek drainage, but limited to non-existent by late summer and early autumn. Higher up, a tarn around 7,100 ft and year-round snow at Burgundy Col are the late-season backups.
bivy.permit: None — no reservation, no quota, no backcountry permit. Northwest Forest Pass for the vehicle at the pullout below.
bivy.capacity: Several established tent spots among the larches; the standard base for the north end of the ridge
